description: Build a credit file on a public or private borrower: capital structure, ratings, how lending funds mark the same loans, financials and key terms. Credit alpha from lender filings.
suggested_questions: Build a credit file on Brightspeed (brightspeed.com), a private company owned by Apollo.
Build a credit file on Optimum Communications (optimum.com), ticker OPTU.
Build a credit file on Pluralsight (pluralsight.com), a private company owned by its former lenders.
skill:
Where credit data lives:
- Borrower identity: the parent, borrower and issuer entities often have different legal names; trade and former
  names matter for search. SEC filer numbers (CIK) exist only for SEC registrants.
- Capital structure: the company's 10-K debt note and credit agreement exhibits when it files; lender presentations;
  rating agency releases (S&P, Moody's, Fitch, KBRA, DBRS Morningstar public press releases); sponsor and arranger
  releases; financing press. Security identifiers (CUSIP, ISIN, loan identifier) appear in fund schedules and filings.
- Lender marks: business development companies and interval funds publish every position in the schedule of
  investments in their 10-Q and 10-K; mutual and closed-end funds in Form N-PORT (no cost field). SEC full-text search
  (efts.sec.gov) finds every fund naming the borrower. Each schedule's header sets its reporting unit (dollars,
  thousands or millions); non-accrual and paid-in-kind status are marked with footnotes.
- Private company financials: rating agency releases, lender filings and press reports of figures given to lenders,
  each labelled as company-reported or third-party estimate.
- Key terms: financial covenants and levels, PIK toggles, guarantors and collateral, unrestricted subsidiaries,
  J.Crew, Serta and Chewy blockers against asset transfers and priming, call protection.

What terms mean:
- Rank: super-priority, first lien, second lien, senior unsecured, subordinated, preferred.
- Fair value below par across several lenders, a mark falling quarter over quarter, or a move to non-accrual is the
  lending market's own read of repayment risk.
- Figures are returned raw, as printed. Ratios, percentages and changes are not computed.

Where the alpha is: BDC schedules show how dozens of lenders value the same private loan every quarter, long before
a rating action or a default headline.

Citations and evidence:
- source_url is one full public https URL: the exact page the value was read on. Never a search results page, an index
  page, an internal file path or a source id. A value from two pages is two values.
- Dates are the date the event happened or the source printed, as YYYY-MM-DD, not today's date.
- Public pages only. Paywalled, logged-in or leaked material, expert-network transcripts and anything marked
  confidential carry MNPI risk and are out of bounds. When only a paywalled article's headline and first lines are
  public, those lines can be used, marked "Headline only:".
- Evidence grades: primary_record (regulator, court, filing, government database, lender schedule, or the live or
  archived page being measured), company_statement, original_press, repeated_press, third_party_tracker. When a page
  repeats a filing, a release or another outlet, the original is the better citation.
- A value nobody published is null. Not an estimate from memory. Analyst opinions, estimates, price targets and
  ratings are views, not evidence.
- Entity drift is the most common error: a namesake, a parent, a subsidiary, a lender or a sister company. Match on
  legal name, ticker, SEC CIK or domain before using a page.
